findings.summary: The er96 wording does not fire the new trigger; the fixture adds the word 'cache' so the test passes.
findings.evidence: Criterion 4 asks for wording from both jobs, including 'an early push whose CI run is reused at landing'. The plan's trigger (1) needs a word from ENV_CACHE_WORDS (cache, cached, artifact...) plus a CI word. Trigger (2) needs a workflow deliverable plus a cache word. The er96 phrase has neither a cache nor an artifact word. The plan's fixture is 'the early commit saves the toolchain cache and its CI run is reused at landing', with a ci.yml deliverable added. System facts and gh/early.rs:23 ('the job of the CI workflow whose pass the host caches') show that reusing the early run's pass is the stored CI result whose ref scope was ignored. As written, a reading in the true er96 shape passes the new cache requirement, and the test cannot show the class is covered. Fix: Make the trigger also fire on reuse of a stored CI result: in one scanned segment, a CI word plus a restore or reuse verb (reuse, reused, restores) plus a result noun (run, pass, result, status). Alternatively, add 'pass' and 'result' with a CI word to the trigger. Use the er96 sentence unchanged in the class test and in a corpus refuse case. Keep an accept control such as 'CI runs the tests', so the trigger stays narrow.
findings.location: Plan Demonstrations, criterion 4 (ii) er96 shape; Steps 1-2 trigger definition

findings.summary: Trigger (2) reads content criteria and the summary, which breaks the check's stated design. The plan does not update that sentence.
findings.evidence: The doc comment says: 'It reads four things and nothing else (not the request, a content criterion, an assumption or out_of_scope, so the repair text cannot trigger it)'. The plan's trigger (2) scans 'any criterion text or the summary' for a cache word. Fixture 3(a) relies on a content criterion ('ci.yml saves a result cache keyed by the fingerprint'). Fix: Either limit trigger (2) to behavior criteria and the summary and use a behavior criterion in fixture 3(a), or reword the 'reads four things' paragraph to list the new inputs and state why content criteria are read for this trigger. Then add an accept control in which a content criterion holds a cache word and there is no workflow deliverable.
findings.location: Plan Step 2 trigger (2); surveys.rs:711-712 doc comment

findings.summary: The CI-word list includes common words, which invites false positives that would inflate the declared 3% share.
findings.evidence: ENV_CI_WORDS includes 'github' and 'actions', and matches lowercase 'ci'. The existing check takes care to need 'CI' written exactly (EnvWord.ci, surveys.rs:417) and words near each other. Under the plan, 'the GitHub API response is cached in memory' or 'the reader caches its actions' would be refused, although neither is a CI cache. Fix: Use 'CI' written exactly (the EnvWord.ci flag), 'workflow' or 'workflows', 'runner' or 'runners', and 'GitHub Actions' as a two-word phrase. Drop bare 'github' and 'actions'. Add these two sentences as accept controls in the unit tests.

findings.summary: The reader's rule line for check_environment_reach is not listed and goes stale. The reader is never told about the new cache-scope requirement before it is refused.
findings.evidence: READING_RULES[5] says: 'Environment: a CI workflow, a push, PR or pull request, or a records-branch or history read needs an `Environment:` assumption: site, read/write permissions, data reached (`check_environment_reach`).' The test the_reader_brief_names_each_reading_rule_in_one_short_line (briefs.rs:4570) limits each line to 220 bytes and the section to 2900 bytes. The reading names the reader stage as an audience. Nothing breaks, but the stage only learns the rule from a refusal and the retry it costs. Fix: Add briefs.rs to the dependents list. Either update the rule line within the 220-byte limit (for example '...; a CI cache or stored result also needs who saves, restores and writes it'), or state in the change description that it is left as a follow-up, since prompt-side text is out of scope.

findings.summary: There is no accept control for meta-wording about the check itself.
findings.evidence: This job's own criteria 3 and 4 contain 'CI cache or artifact' and 'CI run is reused'. Under the plan's trigger they would fire. They pass only because the reading's Environment: assumption happens to hold saved, restored, written and branch. The existing check has environment_reach_accepts_the_criteria_and_summary_of_its_own_job for this case. Fix: Add a test that runs the new check on this job's own criteria and assumptions, as the existing own-job test does, so a later change to the word lists cannot refuse it unnoticed.

summary: I read surveys.rs (check_environment_reach, scan_segments, plain_words, the ENV_* lists), the environment tests and helpers in reading.rs, refusal_corpus.rs (environment_cases, INPUT_FORMS of length 41, environment_reach_refusal_is_declared_intended), replay.rs (replay_declaration) and briefs.rs (READING_RULES). The plan's claims check out: every function, helper and test it names exists, and the only callers of the gate are in athena-core. Fixing the cause inside check_environment_reach is the right place, and the decision not to add a step is sound. One major gap: the trigger is lexical and needs a cache or artifact word. The er96 failure shape, "an early push whose CI run is reused at landing", has no such word. Reusing a CI run's pass across refs is exactly the stored result whose scope the cause is about. The plan's criterion 4 fixture adds "saves the toolchain cache" to the er96 wording so the trigger fires. With the job's real wording the new trigger stays silent, so criterion 4 would not show the class is covered. Smaller points: trigger (2) reads content criteria and the summary, which contradicts the doc comment's design statement, and the plan does not say it updates that statement. The CI-word list includes the common words "github" and "actions". The reader's rule line for Environment in briefs.rs goes stale. Verdict: revise.
